_comment: Mutation survivors accepted as a baseline for the pytest sweep. The nightly ratchet fails when a survivor appears outside this set, and when an entry is no longer a survivor. Regenerate with `python scripts/mutation_gate.py --baseline pytest --update` after a sweep, and only ever let this set shrink. Entries are the survivor line without its line:col position, so they survive unrelated code motion.
survivors: crates/valgebra-py/src/render.rs: replace render_attr_record -> String with String::new()

_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/render.rs: replac: A render arm the shipped surface does not reach. `render_attr_record` writes the `object(field=schema, ...)` form, which is what an `AttrRecord` renders as when it stands alone; every spelling a caller has puts it in a meet with an `Instance`, and `render_meet` reads the class out of that and prints the name. A dataclass, a runtime-checkable protocol, either under `open`, `close` or `simplify`, inside a container, under a double complement -- all of them print the class. So the arm is not undriven, it is unreachable, and no test of the shipped surface can kill this. Bringing it into range means a spelling that builds a bare attribute record, which the frontend has none of.

_accepted.crates/valgebra-py/src/validator.rs: rep: Equivalent: the index is a precompute and every consumer falls back. `ctx.records`, `ctx.attrs`, `ctx.unions` and `ctx.regexes` are each read with `get`, and the arm for a miss computes the answer instead -- `check/walk/scalar.rs` says so where it matters most, compiling a pattern absent from the cache 'on the spot rather than silently passing'. An empty index therefore gives every answer the full one gives, slower. A test cannot tell them apart by any value, and the cost is the instruction gate's business rather than this sweep's.
